CHROMIUM: Add CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_PERMISSIVE_DONTAUDIT It's still useful to have SECURITY_SELINUX_DEVELOP=y by default so that external developers can set their machines to developer mode and set permissive SELinux without having to re-build their kernels, but it's still useful to have it not spam the logs by default due to Chrome OS' large number of permissive rules. This change adds a new flag that lets the user control whether or not to log permissive "denials". Signed-off-by: Luis Hctor Chvez <lhchavez@google.com> BUG=b:33437013 TEST=build with USE=selinux_develop, see lots of logs Change-Id: I53a877ba99ebc4eb040cd7b8c916b0bc3ba48a73 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/424948 Commit-Ready: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Tested-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: config: Re-enable CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_DEVELOP Since the goal of disabling CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_DEVELOP was to reduce logspam, an additional flag has been introduced to do precisely this. Revert "HACK: turn off DDRFreq" This reverts commit 6ea7d249d883362139b2e4b67bc40611c1ce04eb. Resuscitate, resuscitate, resuscitate. Live DDR Freq. Live. Live. Apparently there are problems with suspend / resume and auto power down. We'll "fix" this in the next patch by disabling auto power down for 928 MHz. Since we force DDR Freq to 928 at suspend time then this should avoid the suspend problems until we can root cause. CQ-DEPEND=CL:425839 BUG=chrome-os-partner:61569 TEST=suspend_stress_test --suspend_min=9 --suspend_max=15 Change-Id: I33e85aa7078182e0be62238a6dcadfff2f9f56ce Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425838 Reviewed-by: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: rockchip: disable DDRFreq auto power down at 928 MHz There are currently problems with s2r if we're running with auto power down. We'll "fix" this by disabling auto power down for 928 MHz. Since we force DDR Freq to 928 at suspend time then this should avoid the suspend problems until we can root cause. BUG=chrome-os-partner:61569 TEST=suspend_stress_test --suspend_min=9 --suspend_max=15 Change-Id: Ia61a2207778be4fb6dc9187e1f4f14155cfd5506 Suggested-by: Lin Huang <hl@rock-chips.com> Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425839 Reviewed-by: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org>

cr50: Handle command error on restricted console By default, CR50 uses a restricted console. Most of the commands are restricted. Should perform the unlock process to enable the commands. It is quite a common error for an user who first tries to use CCD. This change prompts an useful message to ask the user to perform the unlock process, instead of returing a timeout error. BUG=chrome-os-partner:58040 TEST=Saw the hint under console locked. $ sudo servod -c ccd_cr50.xml -v 0x18d1 -p 0x5014 $ dut-control ccd_ec_uart_en Problem with ['ccd_ec_uart_en'] :: CCD console is locked. Perform the unlock process! $ dut-control pwr_button Problem with ['pwr_button'] :: CCD console is locked. Perform the unlock process! $ dut-control fw_wp_state Problem with ['fw_wp_state'] :: CCD console is locked. Perform the unlock process! TEST=Saw the commands work fine under console unlocked. Change-Id: Ib51656c5081bd164e22761c26529a0e5aae45fe8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425824 Commit-Ready: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Tested-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Reviewed-by: Nick Sanders <nsanders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org>

ssh_ping: retry on ssh failure This makes ssh_ping not give up on the first ssh error. Currently we see cases in which the "ssh true" command hangs for unknown reasons (DUT is up); no retries are made; the test fails, and the entire build fails. We also need to accept this keyword parameter in servo_host::run(), although this problem is not known to exist for servo_host, and thus we ignore its value for now.
